requirement: Reuse the shared economics while allowing asynchronous-only entry and exit independently.
finding: Async-only modes 4, 8, 12 are implemented with shared accounting.
closure: Retain one signed lifecycle for each single-direction mode; current signed fixtures use both directions.

requirement: Reference mode bits can express the advertised enabled directions; do not silently ignore bits.
finding: CTVS-2 rejects every direct or mixed direct/async mask despite the shared wire allowing 1..15. This is an explicit family subset.
impact: One vault cannot support direct entry with async exit or another mixed mode combination.
closure: Document the supported subset in conformance claims or separately implement mixed modes.

requirement: Keep funding owner, controller, receiver, settler and pauser as separate powers.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:9 (rejects rewritten Claim recipients and missing settler authorization)
finding: Distinct keys/destinations are enforced by their respective branches; controller is not assumed to be receiver.
closure: Add a full signed trace using five distinct roles; existing fixtures reuse some keys.

requirement: Support immutable open-signing-key and sorted authorized-key-set settlement policies.
finding: AnySettler accepts a signing reward key; KeySet additionally checks immutable membership.
closure: Add signed success with an authorized key and signed rejection with an unauthorized key under KeySet.

requirement: Require explicit reward-key signatory membership, including zero-fee batches, with actual ledger witnesses separately checked.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:9 (rejects rewritten Claim recipients and missing settler authorization)
finding: Explicit signatories and actual signature witnesses are distinct checks.
closure: Retain signed zero-reward authorization coverage in addition to predicate coverage.

requirement: Authorized-key identity depends on credential bytes, not the textual spelling of hexadecimal.
finding: The SDK encodes lower/uppercase keys identically but compares KeySet membership using case-sensitive string includes. Uppercase spelling of an authorized key is falsely rejected.
impact: An otherwise permitted batch cannot be planned for semantically identical authorized key bytes.
closure: Normalize byte identities before membership checks and retain a lowercase/uppercase regression. This is an SDK false rejection, not a custody bypass.

requirement: Profile 0 supports exact gross-asset deposits and exact-share redemptions, full fill only.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:29 (port: creation records a funded candidate without State spend or self-reference)
finding: Only the two request kinds are decoded; quoted offered quantity must equal actual escrow value.
closure: Add compiled rejection for an attempted partial-fill remainder output with altered claimed quantities.

requirement: The chain consumption of a request selects settlement, cancellation or expiry, and consumption of a claim selects delivery.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:42 (recovers unsupported economics with controller cancellation and permissionless expiry)
finding: Branches are tied to actual spending-purpose references; no offchain selection authority exists.
closure: Add same-request cancellation-versus-settlement competing transaction traces on a ledger.

requirement: Creating a deposit Request must not change backing or supply.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:29 (port: creation records a funded candidate without State spend or self-reference)
finding: Creation has no State input and no mint; it funds a separate output and labels pending deposit participation.
closure: Add a signed explicit before/after State read for ordinary request creation, rather than inferring from transaction shape.

requirement: Deposit settlement admits net underlying, accrues fee and issues already-participating shares to a funded Claim.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:14 (settles deposits and redemptions into authenticated funded Claims)
finding: The participation cutover is encoded by State and mint changes during Batch, not delivery.
closure: Add a signed delayed-delivery trace across an intervening independent State transition.

requirement: Redemption request creation locks existing participating shares without burning or reducing supply.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:29 (port: creation records a funded candidate without State spend or self-reference)
finding: The planner locks SHARE and carries its participation label; mint is empty.
closure: Add signed request-creation assertions proving supply remains unchanged before settlement.

requirement: Redemption settlement extinguishes shares and fixes a funded net-asset claim outside remaining backing.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:14 (settles deposits and redemptions into authenticated funded Claims)
finding: State debits gross assets, fee accrues, claim contains net underlying and supply burns at settlement.
closure: Add a signed delayed-redemption-claim delivery across later vault activity.

requirement: Delivery only relocates property and must not reprice, mint or consume accounting State.
finding: Q reads claim inputs and fixed destinations; no live vault data or conversion is referenced.
closure: No contract change identified; separately obtain node-backed acceptance.

requirement: Legitimate settlement claims must hold the exact promised asset and quantity plus positive carried ADA.
finding: Claim datum and complete Value are exact outputs derived from economics.
closure: Add independent compiled negative vectors for wrong asset, one-unit economic underpayment, one-unit ADA deficit and unexplained creation surplus.

requirement: Economic-history verification must include balances, supply, fees and claim quantities rather than phase labels alone.
finding: Both printed histories reproduce their distinct arithmetic outcomes. No full state-space lifecycle model or independent reachable-history explorer is present.
impact: Phase-correct traces do not establish arbitrary economic-history correctness.
closure: Retain an economic-state model and compare full traces; prove chosen initial states reachable for each implementation family.

requirement: Do not put authoritative pending queue counts in independently updated State, or close/sweep merely because supply is zero.
finding: State has fixed accounting fields and no queue count or close action. This cited test establishes family dispatch only, not an async residual lifecycle.
closure: Add async last-redemption/residual rebootstrap and unsupported close-action regressions.

requirement: Request identity is the originating output reference learned after construction, not a self-referential datum transaction hash.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:29 (port: creation records a funded candidate without State spend or self-reference)
finding: Identity remains external until construction, then Batch commits predecessor references.
closure: Keep authenticity and indexing requirements distinct from this representation check.

requirement: Candidate creation is not authenticated controller origination, capacity reservation or admission; no request NFT is required.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:29 (port: creation records a funded candidate without State spend or self-reference)
finding: Planner explicitly labels candidate attribution and settlement validates the consumed output. No NFT is added.
closure: Provider disclosure and authenticated origin views remain the separate integration review.

requirement: Dispatch through supported Recovery before downcasting economic_body, including unknown economics and oversized settlement bodies.
finding: Economic_body remains raw Data for Cancel and ExpiryRefund.
closure: Add a property over arbitrary raw bodies at the actual vault endpoint, bounded only by transaction feasibility.

requirement: Unknown outer version, malformed recovery, invalid refund or unsupported controller is not promised recovery.
finding: Exact Recovery decoding and destination validation fail closed; unknown version has actual endpoint coverage.
closure: Add actual endpoint regressions for malformed controller, malformed refund and wrong recovery arity, beyond codec tests.

requirement: Settlement must check vault, Terms, direction, positive input/minimum, funding, budget and full completion.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:186 (eligibility rejects expired, underfunded, wrong-terms and sub-minimum requests)
finding: All predicates appear in the covered-request path; a supported Recovery alone cannot authorize settlement.
closure: Expand compiled negative cases for each predicate independently; current SDK negatives are not compiled evidence.

requirement: Native deposits contain exactly offered underlying and storage plus execution budget, with no other native asset.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:14 (settles deposits and redemptions into authenticated funded Claims)
finding: Closed request Value is compared exactly for native deposits.
closure: Add compiled extra-asset and one-unit underfunding negatives for native deposit requests.

requirement: ADA deposits contain offered ADA plus storage plus execution budget, without counting reserves as backing.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:14 (settles deposits and redemptions into authenticated funded Claims)
finding: ADA components are summed into physical value while pricing only body.offered.
closure: Add compiled reserve-as-economic-input and combined-ADA overflow negatives.

requirement: Redemption escrow contains exact pre-existing SHARE and storage plus budget.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:14 (settles deposits and redemptions into authenticated funded Claims)
finding: Economic input asset is policy SHARE and quantity is the full offered amount.
closure: Add compiled wrong-SHARE-policy/name and surplus-SHARE request cases.

requirement: Carry storage plus unused execution budget minus exact fee plus external top-up to the successful receiver through Claim.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:66 (port: per-request fee, carried ADA, reward signer and both acknowledgment links)
finding: Carried amount is explicit in Claim and its exact physical Value.
closure: Add a compiled theft case that lowers carried ADA while raising settler reward, with balanced aggregate value.

requirement: The exact per-request settler fee cannot exceed budget or be chosen by the executor.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:66 (port: per-request fee, carried ADA, reward signer and both acknowledgment links)
finding: The fee comes only from immutable RequestBody and is summed per request.
closure: Add compiled invalid-budget and fee-increase attempts with otherwise valid transaction allocations.

requirement: Controller cancellation requires the committed key, which may differ from owner and receiver.
finding: The controller is read from Recovery; refund is independently fixed.
closure: Add signed cancellation with distinct funding, controller and refund keys plus absent-controller rejection.

requirement: Protected STATE/ID assets select or reject State dispatch before untrusted Request data can route custody to refund.
finding: Actual input tokens precede Request decoding; State quantity must be exactly one.
closure: Add actual vault-endpoint tests for request-shaped STATE and unexpected ID, rather than only direct recovery helper.

requirement: Reject attached reference scripts on protected Request and Claim inputs and created outputs.
finding: Every protected path has an explicit None reference-script condition.
closure: Retain separate negative tests on source Request, source Claim and created Claim, not only delivery output.

requirement: Extra request assets invalidate settlement but all actual assets remain preserved by supported recovery.
finding: Settlement uses exact Value equality; refund uses a pointwise lower bound across source assets.
closure: Add one paired compiled fixture that fails settlement due only to surplus and succeeds recovery unchanged.

requirement: Price every covered request against the same authenticated pre-settlement State, not a sequentially updated balance.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/settlement.property.test.ts:8 (batch permutations keep one snapshot and allocate every request exactly once)
finding: old State and immutable Terms are reused through all entries.
closure: Add a balanced signed mixed deposit/redemption batch with rounding-sensitive quantities.

requirement: Deposit fees round up on gross input and issued shares round down on net assets using authenticated virtual balances.
finding: Code implements ceil(d*b/(10000+b)) then floor((d-fee)*(S+Vs)/(A+1)).
closure: Preserve independently expected edge vectors including rates 0 and 9999 and minimal positive outcomes.

requirement: Redemption gross assets round down, fees round up on gross assets and payout is gross less fee.
finding: Code implements the printed floor and ceiling formula.
closure: Retain independently expected edge vectors across virtual-share magnitudes and fee boundaries.

requirement: Round each request economic fee separately rather than charging a rounded aggregate.
finding: Each quote is computed within accumulate before fee totals are summed.
closure: Add a split-versus-unsplit example where aggregate rounding differs, at both SDK and compiled levels.

requirement: Every included request must have positive economic input/result and satisfy its minimum output.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:186 (eligibility rejects expired, underfunded, wrong-terms and sub-minimum requests)
finding: Positive gross, net, shares and request minimum are explicit. The SDK rejection test does not exercise compiled failure.
closure: Add compiled zero-output and sub-minimum balanced negative transactions.

requirement: Successor backing adds net deposits and subtracts gross redemptions.
finding: Formula is implemented exactly, including per-request fees outside backing.
closure: Include an adversarial successor with correct supply but wrong backing in compiled tests.

requirement: Successor supply adds gross issued shares and subtracts redeemed shares; accrued fees add entry and exit fees.
finding: Gross totals remain separately accumulated before successor composition.
closure: Add altered-supply and altered-fee successor rejection cases tied to actual State endpoint.

requirement: Native SHARE mint equals net issuance; all other minting is forbidden and nonzero mint is state-coupled.
finding: Whole mint Value is exact, and nonzero mint has a purpose-bound UpdateSupply back-link.
closure: Add signed nonzero mixed batch and compiled unrelated-policy/name mint negatives.

requirement: Physical underlying change equals gross deposits less net payouts, keeping State reserve unchanged.
finding: Exact State and Claim Values plus economic equations enforce the partition under ledger conservation.
closure: A full ledger proof still requires the ledger conservation premise; add independent balanced-theft vectors.

requirement: Bound nonnegative successor balances and participating aggregate economic/physical amounts, including offsetting gross flows.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:147 (port: gross issuance overflow cannot be concealed by same-transaction redemption)
finding: Both gross totals and successor fields are bounded, so netting cannot hide overflow.
closure: Add compiled gross-issued and gross-redeemed overflow cases; existing gross-issued negative is SDK-only.

requirement: Apply max_backing to the final balance, allowing atomic deposit/redemption offsets.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:124 (deposit and redemption price against one old State, with only final-balance cap enforcement)
finding: No undocumented gross deposit cap replaces the final-balance cap.
closure: Add compiled final-cap offset success and over-cap rejection; SDK evidence alone is limited.

requirement: Gross redeemed shares must not exceed old participating supply, even if new issues offset the final supply.
finding: The old supply bound is checked on burned total rather than final net supply.
closure: No source discrepancy identified; signed mixed zero-net evidence remains a separate gate.

requirement: Atomic physical netting is allowed but every request must still receive a fully funded Claim.
finding: No mint-policy invocation is needed for zero net, but State and Requests still validate both gross obligations.
closure: Build a real signed zero-net mixed transaction; current retained zero-net evidence is native endpoint/context testing.

requirement: Deterministic reference ordering is not global FIFO or an all-request fairness promise.
finding: Only selected consumed requests are ordered. No global queue proof or FIFO selection exists.
closure: Keep provider disclosures explicit; do not advertise stronger fairness from these guards.

requirement: Batch entries carry references, output indices and external top-ups only; recompute every economic number.
finding: The validator derives quotes from authenticated Terms and RequestBody, not caller-supplied totals.
closure: Add a mutation corpus around all economic source fields to demonstrate rejection for stale or changed commitments.

requirement: Request acknowledgments require the actual ordinary State input and its StateSpend Batch redeemer.
finding: Reference-only State fails and the redeemer is looked up by Spend(state_ref).
closure: Add retained negatives for real State spent by Pause and TopUpReserve; the positive Batch test does not cover these substitutions.

requirement: Every Request must acknowledge the same exact State reference and Cancel cannot count as settlement acknowledgment.
finding: AcknowledgeBatch is pattern matched in the State Batch path and its state_ref compared.
closure: Add a wrong-but-existing State reference negative alongside the Cancel substitution.

requirement: Cover every consumed P Request exactly once before filtering on economic eligibility.
finding: Count all P inputs other than authentic State, then validate each unique resolved entry.
closure: Add an extra malformed P input omitted from entries, proving invalid candidates cannot be filtered away.

requirement: Entry references are unique, ordered by transaction bytes/index, nonempty and bounded by both max_batch and 16.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:215 (settler authority, batch count and paused direction are independently enforced)
finding: Strict increasing ordering yields uniqueness, and all entries resolve actual input references.
closure: Add actual State endpoint tests at counts 0, 1, 16, 17 and max_batch below the structural maximum.

requirement: State, every Claim and positive reward use distinct in-range output indices, even for identical receivers.
finding: Allocated indices include State and reward before Claims are added.
closure: Add Claim-versus-reward collision and out-of-range output mutations as separate compiled regressions.

requirement: Each Claim binds consumed Request/State refs, vault, Terms, correct result asset/amount, receiver and carried ADA.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:66 (port: per-request fee, carried ADA, reward signer and both acknowledgment links)
reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:9 (rejects rewritten Claim recipients and missing settler authorization)
finding: The expected Claim datum is constructed from authenticated sources and compared structurally.
closure: Add independent wrong-ref, wrong-Terms, wrong-asset and wrong-amount compiled negatives, not just recipient mutation.

requirement: Zero total request fees require no reward output.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:93 (port: zero-net mint retains both gross obligations and deterministic reference order)
finding: None is mandatory when total rewards are zero; SDK disallows reward top-up in that case.
closure: Add compiled zero-fee Some(reward_index) rejection.

requirement: Positive total fees require one ADA-only reward at the signing key enterprise address, NoDatum, no script, value at least exact fees.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:66 (port: per-request fee, carried ADA, reward signer and both acknowledgment links)
finding: All reward address/datum/value predicates appear in the positive branch.
closure: Add compiled wrong-key, underpayment, extra-token, datum and reference-script negatives; happy path alone is not predicate coverage.

requirement: Settlement permits one vault State, its Requests and key funding, rejecting foreign scripts or concurrent Q delivery.
finding: Input scan rejects script credentials other than P; unique_state enforces one STATE-bearing input.
closure: Add signed/compiled foreign-script, second-vault State and concurrent Q input negatives.

requirement: Reject withdrawals including zero, certificates, votes, proposals and treasury fields on protected operations.
finding: Shared allowed_purposes explicitly closes every listed field for all branches.
closure: Run a branch-by-field mutation matrix; only a subset of auxiliary fields has dedicated retained tests.

requirement: Receiving scripts retain exact destinations/datums; producing an output does not execute its spending guard.
finding: Full Address and NoDatum/InlineDatum variants are matched without pretending recipient execution occurred.
closure: Add signed delivery to key-stake and script-stake destination combinations; real recipient reuse is outside profile 0.

requirement: Claim storage is positive and ADA claim physical value is economic lovelace plus carried lovelace.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:14 (settles deposits and redemptions into authenticated funded Claims)
finding: Positive carried reserve and summed ADA quantity are validated before exact output comparison.
closure: Add compiled zero reserve and maximum aggregate ADA boundary regressions.

requirement: Deliver 1..16 Claims at one common Q with one identical semantic delivery list on every Claim input.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:38 (requires all actual Q inputs to agree on one complete delivery list)
finding: Each input redeemer is compared to the same expected Data and full Q input domain is covered. Root-executed signed delivery samples accept 1, 4 and 5 Claims for key and script512 recipients; 6 through 8 exceed memory and 16 exceeds builder size limits.
closure: Add compiled cardinality 0/17 negatives. Retain the signed size-16 failure as measured shape-specific feasibility evidence, then benchmark reference-script and target-node variants rather than treating 16 as a throughput promise.

requirement: Delivery references are unique and exhaustive, and outputs are injectively allocated.
finding: Strict ref ordering, exact count/membership and unique indices jointly close omission and output reuse.
closure: Retain equivalent semantic CBOR list-spelling cases separately in wire review.

requirement: Each delivery preserves every actual input asset including surplus ADA/tokens, never funding fees from Claim property.
finding: Pointwise actual-value preservation is independent of declared economic minimum.
closure: Add a signed surplus Claim delivery whose fee comes from a distinct submitter wallet.

requirement: Delivery may include Claims from different vaults sharing Q without state/config/settler dependencies.
finding: Q payment script defines the domain; no equality constraint on Claim.vault_policy binds the delivery set.
closure: Add a signed two-real-vault Claim delivery; current cross-vault test uses constructed contexts.

requirement: Delivery has no protocol reward, unrelated mint or foreign script-input family.
finding: Full input property must reach destinations; only external funds may become change/fee.
closure: No source discrepancy identified; caller-funded donations are not protocol rewards.

requirement: Funded look-alikes at Q preserve property but must not automatically be treated as authentic vault claims.
finding: Q intentionally validates shape and preservation, not settlement lineage. There is no Claim NFT or State dependence.
closure: The integration-layer reviewer owns authentic lineage and claimable classification; do not infer them from this guard.

requirement: A supported Claim at the common Q guard can be independently delivered.
finding: SDK accepts only enterprise Q source addresses, whereas Q groups any input with its payment script hash. Probe reproduces SDK rejection of the same Q with a staking credential.
impact: Voluntarily funded supported look-alikes at base Q addresses need a custom builder. Genuine Batch Claims remain enterprise and are unaffected.
closure: Either widen the Claim-specific client source check to match Q or explicitly document enterprise-only client support. No compiled staked-Q probe was run.

requirement: Externally funded additions may raise refund or delivery value while preserving the entire source property.
finding: The validators permit >= source value. Public refund/delivery options provide no top-up argument and emit exact source Value.
impact: Minimum-ADA adjustment after protocol changes or voluntary top-ups requires caller-authored plan edits; the default testing builder refuses silent increases.
closure: Expose explicit external top-ups in these planners or document and validate the manual-plan route.

requirement: Direct-at-settlement is a separate explicitly consented native variant, not an alternative spend of existing profile 0 Requests.
finding: Only funded Claim creation is implemented; no alternative disposal branch can be selected.
impact: The optional native variant is unavailable, as permitted by the profile boundary.
closure: A future implementation needs its own profile/mapping, consent, encoding and acceptance evidence; do not retrofit old Request interpretation.

requirement: Cancel/refund consumes exactly one Request plus external key funding, no State, other script family or mint.
finding: The source is the only permitted script input and identity tokens cannot ride other inputs.
closure: Add independent foreign-script, identity-on-key-input, unrelated-mint and forbidden-purpose recovery negatives.

requirement: Refund the immutable full destination and every actual asset, including storage, budget and unexplained surplus.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:42 (recovers unsupported economics with controller cancellation and permissionless expiry)
finding: No fee is removed and no current State is needed.
closure: Add exact refund-datum/staking-credential mutation tests and compiled under-refund of ADA as well as native surplus.

requirement: Controller cancellation remains valid after expiry and does not require settler authorization.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/recovery-delivery.test.ts:17 (port: unsupported economics can be canceled and all surplus property is preserved)
finding: Cancel branch checks controller only and does not compare deadline.
closure: Add actual endpoint and signed after-deadline controller cancellation, beyond the SDK regression.

requirement: Permissionless expiry requires the entire interval at or after deadline and no controller signer.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:42 (recovers unsupported economics with controller cancellation and permissionless expiry)
finding: lower >= deadline is checked and local signed expiry uses a different funding wallet.
closure: Obtain pinned node-backed slot/POSIX boundary evidence.

requirement: Supported validity ranges are finite nonempty lower-inclusive upper-exclusive intervals.
finding: Both finite bounds, inclusivity flags and strict lower<upper are required.
closure: Add lower-open and upper-closed representation negatives and target-ledger slot conversion checks.

requirement: Settlement must fit wholly before the deadline, allowing upper==deadline and rejecting straddling ranges.
finding: Comparison uses interval upper, not wall-clock time.
closure: Add signed boundary cases at non-slot-aligned deadlines under target network slot configuration.

requirement: Only one competing cancel/settle transition can survive per accepted history.
finding: Out-reference consumption gives the intended no-double-spend premise, but no retained competing cancellation/settlement transaction race exists.
impact: The paper A-09 race evidence is not satisfied by isolated successful paths.
closure: Construct both valid candidates against one Request, accept either order, reject the loser, then test rollback/replacement history.

requirement: Entry pause blocks deposit settlement only; exit pause blocks redemption settlement only.
finding: All eight direction/pause combinations pass the review SDK probe; source predicates match. Existing retained compiled corpus does not cover the full matrix.
closure: Add compiled and signed checks for all direction/pause combinations, including unaffected-direction successes.

requirement: Candidate request creation may remain possible while paused and is not admission.
finding: Creation checks enabled mode but does not inspect pause; the probe confirms all pause values permit creation.
closure: Add provider pause/likely-execution disclosure in the required read contract; planner alone does not expose it.

requirement: Pause must not disable existing cancellation, expiry refund or funded-claim delivery.
finding: These paths have no live State/Config dependency and cannot read pause flags.
closure: Add a signed trace that pauses both directions, then cancels, expires and delivers pre-existing objects.

requirement: The printed mixed example must preserve exact backing, supply, fees, mint and per-Request Claim allocations.
finding: Public SDK reproduces A=S=1099500, F=2000, net mint 99500, claims 100000/50000/50000, carried 2 M each, reward 3 M.
closure: Retain this as an independently expected fixture and build a full signed version with measured fees/reserves, not the illustrative fixed network fee.

requirement: The independent delivery, invalid-economics refund, surplus and zero-net examples must preserve their distinct economic meanings.
finding: Equivalent examples are represented across distinct tests; the exact printed numeric set is not all replayed as signed transactions.
closure: Retain a paper-example corpus with separate expected arithmetic and exact signed trace results.

requirement: Managed NAV, lending/ALM deployment, report sequencing, liabilities and real protocol authorization require their own implementation.
finding: No managed State, NAV reporter or strategy adapter exists in profile 0.
impact: Reference validation makes no claim about invested-vault support or recovery from downstream protocols.
closure: Implement and independently verify one pinned managed lifecycle before advertising managed conformance.

requirement: Pending assets cannot be deployed downstream while still advertised as freely refundable escrow.
finding: No in-flight transition exists; allowed Request spends are fixed recovery or full funded settlement.
closure: Add a negative attempt to spend a pending Request into an arbitrary strategy output; integration disclosures must remain explicit.

requirement: Epoch pricing, partial fills, unfunded tickets, transferable Claims and arbitrary routes are deferred extensions.
finding: These features are absent and no optional request field enables them.
closure: Require distinct reviewed ownership/recovery, encoding and complete allocation before any future extension.

requirement: Native inventory accounting needs a separate authenticated issuance/extinction mapping; profile 0 remains mint/burn.
finding: Only coupled native mint/burn is implemented; no inventory adapter is advertised.
closure: Do not infer inventory support from zero-net batch handling.

requirement: Existing Terms, fees, destinations and funded-claim property cannot silently change through governance or migration.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:9 (rejects rewritten Claim recipients and missing settler authorization)
finding: Immutable commitment and exact claims are enforced; there is no governance/migration action.
closure: Add stale/mutated Terms and funded-claim repricing negatives independently of existing recipient tests.

requirement: Batch conservation and rounding must not dilute adjusted price under unchanged external valuation.
finding: Conservation and single-operation rounding properties exist. The cited mixed property checks conservation but does not directly assert equation 13 for arbitrary multi-request batches.
impact: The general batch non-dilution statement lacks a direct retained property/refinement proof.
closure: Add independent multi-request equation 13 and non-dilution properties over feasible bounded batches.

requirement: Funded Claim delivery must remain independent of later solvency, controller and original settler, subject to actual construction feasibility.
finding: Q has no mutable-vault dependencies; source accepts key funding from anyone.
closure: Add signed third-party delivery with controller/settler absent and intervening State activity; network inclusion is not guaranteed.

requirement: Recovery noninterference, complete branch coupling and exclusive delivery must hold together with economics for the same covered sources.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:38 (requires all actual Q inputs to agree on one complete delivery list)
finding: Relevant predicates are implemented jointly rather than as disconnected semantic helpers.
closure: A complete refinement argument and broader balanced adversarial corpus are still absent.

requirement: Keep economic asset fees, execution reward, budget, storage and externally funded transaction costs distinct; recovery/delivery have zero protocol reward.
tests: reference/implementations/ctvs2/client/test/requests-batch.test.ts:66 (port: per-request fee, carried ADA, reward signer and both acknowledgment links)
finding: Planner effects separate asset fees and settler reward; exact property preservation forbids paying recovery fee from escrow.
closure: Expose those distinctions in a user-facing response contract; current plans mark network fee unknown.

requirement: Benchmark increasing batch sizes, worst-case destinations, witnesses and actual parameter limits before release.
finding: New root-executed local signed probes cover ADA/native backing with key or 512-byte script-datum receivers. Sizes 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 pass in every sampled shape; size 8 fails the 14 M memory ceiling. The script/native 7-request case uses 13,898,477 memory. This is a restricted deposit-only sample, not worst-case capacity certification; 16 was not attempted after 8 failed. Separate native-share Claim delivery samples to key or script512 recipients accept 1, 4 and 5 Claims; 6, 7 and 8 fail the 14M memory ceiling. Size 16 fails builder size before signed evaluation: 18,324 bytes for key recipients and 26,964 for script512. The adapter attaches Q.
impact: The structural caps of 16 are not demonstrated executable capacity. Eight ordinary sampled Requests exceed local memory; six sampled Claims exceed memory and sixteen exceed builder size with Q attached.
closure: Retain these measurements and extend to mixed/redeem batches, maximum allowed datum/credential/key/integer/asset shapes, reference-script delivery and target-node parameters. Do not treat sampled maxima 7 and 5 as universal safe capacities.

requirement: Reject excessive supported request/destination data before an SDK user locks funds.
tests: reference/packages/protocol/tests/wire.test.ts:235 (keeps cancellation recovery available for unsupported and oversized economic bodies)
finding: SDK creation validates supported bounded data; raw third-party output creation remains unrestricted by a spending script.
closure: Do not advertise all schema-valid outputs as necessarily resource-feasible; measure complete supported transactions.

requirement: Evaluate actual signed transaction bytes and required witnesses with real context instead of promoting synthetic semantic inputs to ledger proof.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:14 (settles deposits and redemptions into authenticated funded Claims)
finding: Local signed CBOR is checked, including witnesses, declared budgets and actual Plutus execution. Full cardano-node phase 1 is not exercised.
impact: Local acceptance cannot establish public-network acceptance or every ledger prerequisite.
closure: Run equivalent node-backed traces with a named era and parameter snapshot.

requirement: Demonstrate multiple independent request creations without consuming State.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:38 (requires all actual Q inputs to agree on one complete delivery list)
finding: Two funded deposit Requests precede one settlement in the signed local fixture.
closure: Add concurrent independent wallets and explicit unchanged State reference assertions.

requirement: Demonstrate ADA/native/share funding partitions and malformed request rejection.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:14 (settles deposits and redemptions into authenticated funded Claims)
finding: Both backing assets and both request kinds execute locally; malformed economic constructor is rejected natively.
closure: Complete the compiled malformed-value and each-field matrix; do not substitute SDK rejection for script rejection.

requirement: Demonstrate actual controller key witnesses separately from capability extension guards.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:42 (recovers unsupported economics with controller cancellation and permissionless expiry)
finding: Positive controller cancellation and another-wallet expiry have signatures; missing-controller negative is a predicate test.
closure: Add cryptographic missing/incorrect controller witness rejection through node-backed validation; capability profile remains out of scope.

requirement: Demonstrate full-only settlement rejects omitted sources, duplicate refs and hidden remainder.
finding: Omission and duplicate cases exist; no dedicated balanced hidden-remainder transaction is retained.
closure: Add compiled partial-fill/remainder attempts and complete signed rejection evidence.

requirement: Demonstrate mixed snapshot pricing, wrong checkpoint rejection and per-request fee rounding.
finding: Mixed arithmetic is covered; no signed mixed wrong-State-basis corpus or split-fee-versus-aggregate compiled fixture is retained.
closure: Add those three independently expected economic vectors at the transaction layer.

requirement: Demonstrate gross supply conservation and zero-net mint without relying on mint-policy execution.
finding: Native entrypoint contexts establish gross checks; no retained signed mixed zero-net transaction exists.
closure: Construct and submit a zero-net batch from authentic prior Requests with final signed evaluation.

requirement: Demonstrate same-receiver allocation, repeated-index rejection and no overlapping reserves.
finding: Repeated indices are tested in settlement and delivery. Full reserve-overlap mutation coverage remains incomplete.
closure: Add balanced reserve theft and Claim/reward collision transaction vectors.

requirement: Demonstrate exact funded immutable Claims, including wrong asset/quantity/datum rejection and no delivery repricing/mint.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:9 (rejects rewritten Claim recipients and missing settler authorization)
finding: Recipient and mint negatives exist; independent wrong asset/quantity and all credential/datum shapes are not all retained.
closure: Add the missing compiled field/value mutation matrix and delayed-delivery history.

requirement: Demonstrate exact deadline boundaries and cancellation/settlement races.
finding: Boundary predicate tests and one local expiry trace exist; races and node-backed slot conversion do not.
closure: Add competing spends and target-node interval edge tests.

requirement: Demonstrate unauthorized operators fail and authorized operators cannot violate economics.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:9 (rejects rewritten Claim recipients and missing settler authorization)
finding: KeySet membership negative is native context; signed economic recipient mutation and missing required signer are rejected.
closure: Add fully signed authorized-KeySet economic attack and unauthorized-KeySet transaction cases.

requirement: Demonstrate fixed delivery with controller/batcher offline and multi-Claim output uniqueness.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:38 (requires all actual Q inputs to agree on one complete delivery list)
finding: No signer is required by Q; signed multi-Claim success exists, but a distinct third-party delivery/offline-role scenario is not retained.
closure: Use another wallet to deliver authentic Claims while all original roles are absent.

requirement: Managed NAV/liability conformance needs stale-report, overlap and post-report-flow evidence.
finding: No managed profile is claimed or implemented.
closure: Keep this requirement open for a future managed mapping rather than marking it passed by direct-custody tests.

requirement: Demonstrate settlement rollback, delivery-only rollback and competing replacement histories.
finding: No production lifecycle indexer or retained rollback/replay corpus exists.
impact: Authenticated async history cannot yet be reconstructed robustly across reorganizations.
closure: Implement coherent lifecycle projection and branch-replay tests; detailed interface review belongs to the root integration report.

requirement: Demonstrate measured worst-case batches, datums, reserves, fees and witnesses.
finding: New root-executed local signed probes cover ADA/native backing with key or 512-byte script-datum receivers. Sizes 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 pass in every sampled shape; size 8 fails the 14 M memory ceiling. The script/native 7-request case uses 13,898,477 memory. This is a restricted deposit-only sample, not worst-case capacity certification; 16 was not attempted after 8 failed. Separate native-share Claim delivery samples to key or script512 recipients accept 1, 4 and 5 Claims; 6, 7 and 8 fail the 14M memory ceiling. Size 16 fails builder size before signed evaluation: 18,324 bytes for key recipients and 26,964 for script512. The adapter attaches Q.
impact: The structural caps of 16 are not demonstrated executable capacity. Eight ordinary sampled Requests exceed local memory; six sampled Claims exceed memory and sixteen exceed builder size with Q attached.
closure: Retain these measurements and extend to mixed/redeem batches, maximum allowed datum/credential/key/integer/asset shapes, reference-script delivery and target-node parameters. Do not treat sampled maxima 7 and 5 as universal safe capacities.

requirement: Two independent decoders, builders and indexers must agree on authenticated transaction histories.
finding: There is one public planning implementation and one local Lucid ledger adapter; CLI parameter comparison is not an independent transaction builder or indexer.
impact: Independent interoperability acceptance is not closed.
closure: A separate author/toolchain must reconstruct real histories and effects without calling these builders.

requirement: Historical publication/model/wire evidence and preserved source-bundle claims must not be promoted into new execution certification.
finding: Current validation differentiates local execution from historic evidence. Original candidate-wire and assurance register artifacts remain unavailable.
impact: Exact historical fixture reconciliation and evidence-register closure cannot be claimed.
closure: Obtain the referenced source bundle and compare its byte-level fixtures and requirement registers independently.

requirement: Prove a real-transaction projection from ledger prerequisites plus compiled acceptance to all applicable CTVS requirements, with intended negative failure reasons.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/guards.test.ts:9 (rejects rewritten Claim recipients and missing settler authorization)
finding: Entry points inspect actual contexts and negative tests must reach evaluator, but reaching an evaluator failure alone does not identify its precise semantic predicate. No complete refinement proof exists.
impact: Passing examples and high TypeScript coverage do not establish universal soundness.
closure: Record predicate-specific counterexamples/traces and provide independent model-to-validator refinement evidence.

requirement: Execute the full declared acceptance trace including authenticated deployment, requests, mixed/zero-net settlement, script destinations, recovery, maintenance and external interoperability.
tests: reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:14 (settles deposits and redemptions into authenticated funded Claims)
reference/testing/integration/ctvs2/lifecycle.test.ts:42 (recovers unsupported economics with controller cancellation and permissionless expiry)
finding: Local ADA/native sequential lifecycle, maintenance, recovery and multi-Claim paths exist; new root probes add deposit-only batch sizes through 7 and final Claim delivery to key and script512 receivers through 5. The async family deliberately lacks direct deposit. Signed mixed zero-net, node-backed, independent-builder and rollback portions remain open.
impact: The combined trace printed in the paper cannot be completed inside this single async-only family.
closure: State the family-specific trace substitution explicitly and complete all remaining applicable acceptance legs.

requirement: Script-controlled protocol users and real managed integrations need their actual guards and successor tests.
finding: Sending to a script destination is supported but does not demonstrate that script-controller capability or managed integration.
closure: Implement real pinned integrations before making those separately scoped claims.
